title: Minimizing Surface Area of a Cylindrical Can
author: Muhammad Abdullah Athar
problemStatement: A cylindrical can must hold 1000 cm^3 of liquid. Find the radius r and height h that minimize the total surface area.

steps.title: Relate Volume and Surface Area
steps.mathExpression: V = \pi r^2 h = 1000 \implies h = \frac{1000}{\pi r^2}; \quad A = 2\pi r^2 + 2\pi rh = 2\pi r^2 + 2\pi r\left(\frac{1000}{\pi r^2}\right) = 2\pi r^2 + \frac{2000}{r}
steps.explanation: Substitute h into total surface area (two circular ends plus lateral jacket).

steps.title: Differentiate with Respect to r
steps.explanation: Set A'(r) = 0 and solve for r.

steps.title: Solve for Height h
steps.explanation: Notice the optimal cylindrical can always has height equal to its diameter (h = 2r).
steps.why: Universal geometric optimality condition for cylinders.
